title: What is a chatbot actually doing?
question: How does ChatGPT work?
summary: A chatbot is a program that predicts text. When you send a message, it reads it as small pieces called tokens. It then works out which piece is likely to come next, adds it, and repeats, one piece at a time, until the reply is finished. This episode follows a single reply from start to end.

claims.claim: A chatbot builds its reply one token at a time.
A token is often a whole word, or part of one.
At each step, the model scores many possible next tokens and picks one.
Asked the same question twice, the same chatbot can give different replies.

bridge: You now know a chatbot writes one piece at a time. Next: what those pieces are.
